message.content: I've reviewed the full contract and kernel source. This is an exact-integer affine recurrence solved with a three-pass chunked scan (local `associative_scan` over 8-step blocks, an exclusive tree scan over chunk summaries, then a carry-application pass). I traced the tree-scan structure (up-sweep with aligned endpoints, identity reset at lane C-1, down-sweep where each lane is written once as `left` and once as `right`, with no write-order conflict) and it appears structurally sound, including the C=1/LEVELS=0 and CHUNKS<C padding cases. I'll record the description model with the residual risk surfaces for Skeptic.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Compute state = matrix[row,step] @ state + bias[row,step] for every step, per batch row; output fresh int64 [B,N,2] on the input device.", "Exact integer arithmetic only: atol=0, rtol=0; no modulo, saturation or approximation; int64 must hold every result (contract asserts max state magnitude < 2^48).", "Public domain: matrix int8 [B,N,2,2] with entries in {-1,0,1}; bias int16 [B,N,2]; initial int16 [B,2] with all int16 values legal; 1<=B<=64, 1<=N<=32; singular/noncommuting matrices allowed; no distribution or seed restrictions.", "Inputs are dense, contiguous, strided, same CUDA device; nonzero storage offsets and shared storage are legal; requires_grad/is_inference/is_neg/is_conj all false; ordinary non-inference mode.", "validate_inputs() enforces the domain and is called by run(); reference() is a sequential int64 recurrence that also accepts CPU; make_inputs() is examples only.", "Correctness is a single verdict for the whole implementation; any single legal input demonstrating a mismatch is decisive."], "kernel_model":
function.name: record_description_update
